group_scores.rationale: The policy signals point both ways. Ueda (19 Nov, verified) said the BoJ will keep hiking from 1.25%, and Takata dissented for 1.5%. Core CPI is 2.2% and the 20y auction (verified) was orderly. Against that, Q3 GDP was -0.1% annualised against a +0.2% consensus, and AI and chip stocks sold off on 17 and 20 Nov. Round-2 T3 prices show the Nikkei at about -7.7% and the Topix at about -7.1% on the week, with banks down about 11%. T1 data show foreign net selling in the 2nd week of November, and USD/JPY flat at about 159.2-159.9 with no MoF FX remarks. The broad price drop leans negative, but the lead kept 0, and the drop is a global AI de-rating, not a Japan-specific shift. The verifier does not raise scores. Unsaturated: capped at |1|, low.
group_scores.falsifier: T1/T2 evidence that the Topix drawdown is Japan-specific (foreign selling 16-20 Nov from JPX on 26 Nov), or MoF intervention or a December hike driving a yen rally of 3% or more.
